decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 2.5%. The vote was 12-0.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 2-1/2 percent.

The Committee believes that, even after this action, the stance of monetary policy remains accommodative and, coupled with robust underlying growth in productivity, is providing ongoing support to economic activity.
The Committee perceives the upside and downside risks to the attainment of both sustainable growth and price stability for the next few quarters to be roughly equal.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 13.02% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.15% and moved 0 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.67% would not change.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 5.4%, and employers added an average of 180k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.3% over the past year (December 2004); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +3 bp on the day.
